schema.description: The Head's seven-row taxonomy as columns of one table, every arm and both controls on every row, byte ledger asserted per row.

value_holdout_scope: SCOPE OF THE VALUE HOLD-OUT (⛔ quote no row without this). The hold-out is from the STORE'S FIT POOL, not from the encoder, the decoder or the judge. Those three are frozen, hash-pinned and read-only (charter §A.4) and were fitted on a train split containing EVERY hue and EVERY shape; re-fitting them on a value hold-out would void every wave-2 number and is out of scope. Therefore 'never trained on' means here: THE STORE NEVER HELD A ROW CARRYING THAT VALUE. The decoder can still render the value and the judge can still recognise it — which is what makes rows 2/5/6/7 scorable at all. ⛔ Read end-to-end, 'never seen' is false and the claim dies with it.

r7_deletion.why: ⭐ THE strongest instrument. Deleting a value from the store does not move the factor grid, so the no-model rule's delta_reject is exactly 0.0. A changed refusal after a deletion, with NO retraining, is not producible by any syntactic rule.

r5_comp_refusal.why: ⭐ Evidential UNDER THE AMENDED PAIRING ONLY: the accept-leg is row 1, a STORED on-grid request. Both halves are well-formed on-grid requests and differ only in whether the store holds the value. ⛔ With row 2 as the accept-leg it was free (grid look-up, 1.0000, zero bytes).

r6_invalid_refusal.why: ⛔ SANITY CHECK ONLY, and it can never be anything else: out-of-range is decidable from the factor grid alone. Kept as the degenerate-arm guard; ⛔ a row-6 number is NOT evidence that the store computes a barrier.

amendment_1: ⭐ Row 5's accept-leg is ROW 1 (a stored, on-grid value), ⛔ not row 2. Row 2 is accept-only and is consumed by no refusal row. Row 6 is `evidential: false` — a sanity check, never evidence for the store. Row 7's delta_reject is the programme's strongest instrument: deleting a value does not move the factor grid, so a no-model rule's delta is 0.0.

controls.note: ⭐ basis+head (the wave-2 object) is the FIRST control and the like-for-like; knn_proto is the second row; the grid-syntax rule is the no-model laundering control on the refusal rows.
